metaDescription: Budget conference speakerphones compared on microphone pickup, USB and Bluetooth, noise reduction and battery, so small-room calls sound clear.
expertTake: The Jabra Speak 510 is the best overall budget pick because it pairs a proven speaker and microphone with both USB and Bluetooth, and the Anker PowerConf S330 is the value pick for a simple home office desk. Anyone who regularly meets with more than a handful of people in a large room should look beyond this category to a dedicated room system.
introParagraphs: A conference speakerphone is a speaker and a microphone array in one puck, built so a few people around a table or a desk can hear and be heard on a call. At the budget end the differences that matter are microphone pickup, how well the unit suppresses echo and background noise and how it connects.

This guide focuses on the lower half of the price range and is honest about the limits. We evaluated each model from published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, with attention to pickup range, battery behaviour and year-three reliability. Speakerphones are sized for small rooms, and no puck can fix a large, echoey space.

products.name: Jabra Speak 510 portable USB and Bluetooth speakerphone
products.description:
The Jabra Speak 510 is a portable speakerphone that connects over USB or Bluetooth, which makes it flexible for a laptop on a desk or a phone in a hallway meeting. The design approach is a compact puck with an omnidirectional microphone and a speaker tuned for speech, plus simple controls for volume and muting. Jabra's brand track record in this category is the main reason it tops the list.

Compared with the Speak 410, the 510 adds Bluetooth, which removes the cable from the table. Compared with the Anker S330, it is better for groups of a few people but costs more. It is not built for a large conference table, and for rooms beyond a small huddle space you will want a bigger system.

Ownership is easy. Charge it, pair it once and keep the USB cable handy for when Bluetooth is not ideal. Wipe the speaker grille with a dry cloth, and keep the firmware updated through the maker's software if you use it often. Place it in the middle of the table rather than at one end, because the microphone hears evenly only when everyone sits at a similar distance.
products.bestFor: Small groups and mobile workers who want USB and Bluetooth flexibility.

products.name: Anker PowerConf S330 USB speakerphone, plug and play
products.description:
The Anker PowerConf S330 is the simplest and cheapest speakerphone in this lineup, built for home offices and small meetings. It connects over USB and uses a conference microphone array to pick up a few voices around a desk. The design approach is plug-and-play with no battery management, which keeps the product straightforward.

Compared with the Jabra Speak 510, the S330 lacks Bluetooth, so it ties you to a cable. Compared with the Yealink SP92, it has a smaller feature list and no noise reduction or certification, but a lower price and simpler setup. It is a good fit for someone who takes video calls from a desk and occasionally has a colleague join.

Ownership requires little. Plug it in, set it as the default audio device and check the volume. Keep the cable tidy, and wipe the grille occasionally. If the microphone sounds quiet, check the operating system input level rather than blaming the unit. Because it draws power from the computer, a laptop on battery will drain a little faster during a long call, so keep the charger nearby.

products.name: Yealink SP92 Teams certified speakerphone, AI noise reduction
products.description:
The Yealink SP92 is a Microsoft Teams certified speakerphone with AI noise reduction and a long battery life listed at around 20 hours. The design approach is to handle noisy rooms by filtering background sound before it reaches the call. For offices that standardize on Teams, certification means the buttons and call controls work out of the box.

Compared with the Jabra Speak 510, the SP92 leans harder on noise reduction and certification, while the Jabra leans on brand polish and portability. Compared with the Lenovo, it adds a more mature conferencing brand but costs a little more. It is a good fit for a small room where fan noise or street noise would otherwise intrude.

Ownership is simple. Charge it fully before long days and keep a USB cable on hand. Check the maker's software for firmware updates, and clean the grille with a dry cloth. If the noise reduction seems aggressive on music, switch to a mode that suits your calls. Set the noise reduction level in the maker's software before an important call, since the strongest setting can clip soft speech.

products.name: Lenovo Teams certified Bluetooth conference speakerphone
products.description:
The Lenovo speakerphone is a Teams certified Bluetooth unit aimed at offices and home workers. It combines a wireless connection with certified controls, so it works with Teams without extra setup. The design approach is straightforward: a compact body, call controls and a speaker tuned for voices.

Compared with the Yealink SP92, the Lenovo costs a little less and has a smaller feature list. Compared with the Jabra Speak 510, it is less established in the category but comparable in concept. It makes sense as a company-standard pick for Lenovo laptops and Teams users.

Ownership is minimal. Pair it, charge it and check the firmware. Clean the speaker grille with a dry cloth, and keep it away from heat. If Bluetooth drops, try re-pairing or move the unit closer to the computer. Pair it before the meeting starts and check the volume on both ends, because a first-time Bluetooth connection is not the moment to troubleshoot.

products.name: Jabra Speak 410 USB corded speakerphone, plug and play
products.description:
The Jabra Speak 410 is an older, corded USB speakerphone that remains a dependable choice for desk calls. The design approach is simple: plug it in, set it as the audio device and take calls. There is no battery and no Bluetooth, so reliability is its main selling point.

Compared with the Speak 510, the 410 is cheaper but ties you to a cable. Compared with the Anker S330, it has a longer track record but a more dated look. It suits an office desk where the computer stays put and you want a unit that just works.

Ownership is trivial. Keep the cable from kinking, wipe the grille and check the volume in the operating system. Because it is older, firmware updates are rare, so what you buy is what you get. Keep the cable out of the walking path, since a tug on the cord is the most common way a corded unit ends up on the floor.
products.bestFor: Desk workers who want a reliable corded speakerphone.

No battery to wear out or charge
Jabra reputation for speech clarity in small groups
Plug-and-play with most computers and softphones
cons: Older design with fewer modern features

buyingCriteria.explanation: A single omnidirectional microphone suits one or two people at a desk, while an array of several microphones can cover a table of four to six. The Jabra Speak 510 uses a single omnidirectional microphone and the Anker S330 a small conference array, so both are sized for a desk or a small huddle. The mistake is expecting a single puck to cover a large conference table, and no puck at this tier replaces a ceiling or table microphone system for a bigger group.

Full duplex audio lets both sides talk at once, and noise reduction filters fans and keyboard clicks. The Yealink SP92 uses AI noise cancelling, while the Jabra units rely on tuned speech processing. Hard rooms with glass and bare walls cause echo that no budget puck fully fixes, so soft furnishings matter as much as the device.

USB is the most reliable connection and powers the unit from the computer. Bluetooth removes the cable but adds pairing and battery management. The Jabra Speak 510 offers both, while the Speak 410 and Anker S330 are USB only. Choose based on whether the device will move between rooms. Bluetooth range is usually short, so keep the unit within a few metres of the computer to avoid dropouts mid-call.

Teams and Zoom certification mean the buttons and call controls integrate with those apps. The Yealink SP92 and Lenovo are Teams certified. If your company uses a particular platform, certification saves setup time, but it is not required for basic audio.

Battery life matters for wireless units. The Yealink lists around 20 hours, which covers long days, while USB-only models have no battery to wear out. Batteries lose capacity over time, so a unit that can run from USB is more future-proof. If you rely on battery power, plan a charge after each long day rather than waiting for the unit to run flat.

Speakerphones are sized for small rooms. A desk or a table of three to four people is the sweet spot for single pucks, and a table of five or six is about the limit even for the better units here, such as the Yealink SP92. Beyond that, a ceiling microphone or room system is a better fit than a bigger puck, and adding a second unit is rarely as clean as it sounds.

howWeEvaluated.title: Microphone coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared microphone designs and what owners say about pickup range. The Yealink SP92 and Anker S330 lead on array features, while the Jabra Speak 510 suits small groups. We weighted coverage highly for meeting rooms.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speech clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: We read feedback on speaker tuning and echo handling. Jabra's speech tuning gets steady praise, while the Yealink's noise cancelling draws mixed notes. Room acoustics changed every result.

howWeEvaluated.title: Connection and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at USB and Bluetooth behaviour and what owners say about pairing. The USB-only models are the most reliable, while Bluetooth units add pairing steps. Setup simplicity was a key score.

howWeEvaluated.title: Certification and software
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered Teams certification and support software. The Yealink and Lenovo carry Teams certification, while the Jabra and Anker work as generic audio devices. Software updates were treated as a bonus.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value in context
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each unit in the lower half of the price range and asked what it gives up. The Anker is the cheap, simple choice, the Jabra Speak 510 is the all-rounder and the Yealink gives the best noise handling and certification. Battery wear on wireless models was a long-term concern.

faq.q: Is a speakerphone better than a headset?
faq.a: A speakerphone is better for groups, while a headset is better for a single person in a noisy area. For desk calls with one person, a headset usually gives clearer audio. If you share the room with others who are not on the call, a headset keeps your conversation private, which a speakerphone cannot do.

faq.q: How much should a budget speakerphone cost?
faq.a: Prices move, so check the current listing. The simplest USB models are the cheapest, Bluetooth and certified units sit in the middle, and larger kits cost more. Pay for features you will actually use.

faq.q: How many people can a speakerphone cover?
faq.a: Single pucks suit one to four people, while the better units like the Yealink SP92 stretch to five or six. Beyond that, a dedicated room system or a ceiling microphone is a better fit, because a puck on a long table leaves the far end of the room too distant from the microphones to be understood reliably.

It matters if you use Teams and want integrated call buttons. The audio quality does not change, so skip it if you use other platforms. Check that your meeting app lists the device in its audio settings, since a certified unit still needs to be selected as the speaker and microphone.

Hard walls and glass reflect sound back into the microphone. Soft furnishings, a smaller room or a unit with better echo cancellation help. Placing the unit away from walls also reduces echo. Soft furnishings such as a rug, curtains or a bookshelf behind the speaker absorb a surprising amount of reflected sound.
USB is more reliable and powers the unit, while Bluetooth is more flexible. If the unit stays on one desk, USB is the safer choice.
